content_voiceover: This slide covers Hodgkin lymphoma prognostic factors, and it splits cleanly into early stage versus advanced stage systems, which boards love to test separately. For early stage, meaning stage I to II disease, three cooperative groups, the German Hodgkin Study Group, the EORTC, and the NCCN, each define unfavorable risk factors that determine whether a patient gets combined modality therapy versus chemotherapy alone. The factors overlap heavily: elevated ESR combined with B symptoms, a large mediastinal mass measured as a mediastinal mass ratio greater than about a third, more than two or three involved nodal sites depending on the group, extranodal extension called an E lesion, and bulky disease generally over ten centimeters. You don't need to memorize every cutoff by group, but you should recognize the categories: age, ESR plus B symptoms, mediastinal bulk, nodal sites, and E lesions. For advanced stage disease, the tool is the International Prognostic Score, the IPS, which assigns one point per adverse factor, seven factors total, and is remembered with the mnemonic A2S2L2H: albumin under 4, age over 45, stage IV disease, male sex, leukocytosis over 15,000, lymphocytopenia under 600 or under 8 percent of the white count, and hemoglobin under 10.5. Higher IPS scores correlate with worse progression-free and overall survival and increasingly guide treatment intensification.
keypoints: Early stage (I-II): GHSG, EORTC, NCCN unfavorable risk factors
Unfavorable factors: high ESR + B symptoms, bulky mediastinal mass, >2-3 nodal sites, E lesion
Advanced stage: International Prognostic Score (IPS), 1 point per factor, 7 factors
Mnemonic A2S2L2H: Albumin<4, Age>45, Stage IV, Sex male, Leukocytosis>15K, Lymphocytopenia, Hgb<10.5
keypoint_voiceover: Two systems to separate clearly. Early stage one and two disease uses unfavorable risk factors from GHSG, EORTC, and NCCN: think high ESR with B symptoms, bulky mediastinal mass, and multiple nodal sites. Advanced stage disease uses the International Prognostic Score, one point each for seven factors, best remembered as A2S2L2H: albumin under 4, age over 45, stage IV, sex male, leukocytosis over 15,000, lymphocytopenia, and hemoglobin under 10.5.
